title: Bearer Cards and Account-Bound Credit in Gift Cards & Store Credit
content:
Gift Cards & Store Credit instruments fall into two holding kinds. An account-bound instrument lives only in the holder's account wallet and has no card number to share; a bearer card has a card number and PIN, can be given to and registered by another customer, and needs its PIN to be spent online.

| Instrument type | Account-bound (wallet only, no card number) | Can be given to and registered by another customer | Can be registered to a profile with card number and PIN | PIN needed with the card number to spend online |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marlowe Rewards Note | Yes | No | No | No |
| Bonus Gift Card | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Goodwill Credit | Yes | No | No | No |
| Return Store Credit | Yes | No | No | No |
| Marlowe & Finch Gift Card | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Questions answered from the table

**Which types are bearer cards?** The Bonus Gift Card, the Marlowe & Finch Gift Card and the Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card. Each of them has all three bearer properties: transferable, registrable and PIN-protected online.

**Can a Goodwill Credit or a Return Store Credit be passed to another customer?** No. Both are account-bound, with no card number, and neither is transferable to another customer or registrable to another profile. The same holds for the Marlowe Rewards Note.

**When is a PIN needed?** Only for the three bearer types, and only when the card number is used to spend online. Account-bound instruments have no PIN requirement because they have no card number.
